name: Add Dependency
description: Add Dependency Set a task as waiting on or blocking another task. POST /api/v2/task/{task_id}/dependency
context:
POST /api/v2/task/{task_id}/dependency
Set a task as waiting on or blocking another task.
Required: task_id (path) — This is the task which is waiting on or blocking another task.; body (body) — Use the `depends_on` parameter in the request body to specify the task that must be completed before the task in the path parameter.\ \ Use the `dependency_of` parameter in the request body to specify the task that's waiting for the task in the path parameter to be completed.\ \ You can only use one per request.
Optional: custom_task_ids (query) — If you want to reference a task by it's custom task id, this value must be `true`.; team_id (query) — When the `custom_task_ids` parameter is set to `true`, the Workspace ID must be provided using the `team_id` parameter. \ For example: `custom_task_ids=true&team_id=123`.

name: Get Task
description: Get Task View information about a task. GET /api/v2/task/{task_id}
context:
GET /api/v2/task/{task_id}
View information about a task. You can only view task information of tasks you can access. \ \ Tasks with attachments will return an "attachments" response. \ \ Docs attached to a task are not returned.\ \ The `custom_fields` array only includes Custom Fields applicable to the task's `custom_item_id`. Use [Get Custom Fields](ref:getaccessiblecustomfields) and each field's `applied_objects` to discover which fields apply to which task types.
Required: task_id (path)
Optional: custom_task_ids (query) — If you want to reference a task by its custom task id, this value must be `true`.; team_id (query) — When the `custom_task_ids` parameter is set to `true`, the Workspace ID must be provided using the `team_id` parameter. \ For example: `custom_task_ids=true&team_id=123`.; include_subtasks (query) — Include subtasks, default false; include_markdown_description (query) — To return task descriptions in Markdown format, use `?include_markdown_description=true`.; custom_fields (query) — Include tasks with specific values in one or more Custom Fields. Custom Relationships are included.\ \ For example: `?custom_fields=[{"field_id":"abcdefghi12345678","operator":"=","value":"1234"},{"field_id":"jklmnop123456","operator":"<","value":"5"}]`\ \ Only set Custom Field values display in the `value` property of the `custom_fields` parameter. If you want to include tasks with specific values in only one Custom Field, use `custom_field` instead.\ \ Learn more about [filtering using Custom Fields.](doc:filtertasks)

name: Get Task Comments
description: Get Task Comments View task comments. GET /api/v2/task/{task_id}/comment
context:
GET /api/v2/task/{task_id}/comment
View task comments. \ \ Retrieve comments from a task. Results are returned in reverse chronological order (newest to oldest). By default, the request returns the 25 most recent comments.\ \ [Pagination](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/task-comments-pagination): To fetch the next page of history (older comments), you must use the `start` and `start_id` parameters together, using the data from the last comment of the current response.
Required: task_id (path)
Optional: custom_task_ids (query) — If you want to reference a task by it's custom task id, this value must be `true`.; team_id (query) — When the `custom_task_ids` parameter is set to `true`, the Workspace ID must be provided using the `team_id` parameter. \ For example: `custom_task_ids=true&team_id=123`.; start (query) — The Unix timestamp (in milliseconds) of the reference comment. Required for pagination. Must be used in combination with `start_id`. \ Value should be the `date` of the last comment from the previous response.; start_id (query) — The unique ID of the reference comment. Required for pagination. Must be used in combination with `start`. \ Value should be the `id` of the last comment from the previous response.

name: Set Custom Field Value
description: Set Custom Field Value Add data to a Custom field on a task. POST /api/v2/task/{task_id}/field/{field_id}
context:
POST /api/v2/task/{task_id}/field/{field_id}
Add data to a Custom field on a task. \ \ You'll need to know the `task_id` of the task you want to update, and the universal unique identifier (UUID) `field_id` of the Custom Field you want to set. \ \ The Custom Field must be applicable to the task's current `custom_item_id`. Use [Get Custom Fields](ref:getaccessiblecustomfields) (check each field's `applied_objects`) or [Get Task](ref:gettask) to find applicable `field_id` values.\ \ Returns `400` if the field is not enabled for the task's custom task type.
Required: task_id (path) — Enter the task ID of the task you want to update.; field_id (path) — Enter the universal unique identifier (UUID) of the Custom Field you want to set.; body (body)
Optional: custom_task_ids (query) — If you want to reference a task by its Custom Task ID, this value must be `true`.; team_id (query) — When the `custom_task_ids` parameter is set to `true`, the Workspace ID must be provided using the `team_id` parameter. \ For example: `custom_task_ids=true&team_id=123`.
